name: Wave Sprint Timeline Template
description: Per-wave program activity sequence and sprint timeline templates based on proven global pharma CRM deployment patterns. Use alongside the Multi-Country Rollout Planner to build detailed wave-level execution plans.

standard_wave.name: Standard Wave (16-20 weeks)
standard_wave.description: Standard timeline for a single wave deploying to one region. Suitable for most waves in a multi-wave program.

activities: Scope alignment with country stakeholders
Country-specific regulatory requirements gathering
Data model delta analysis (what differs from prior waves)
Custom solution gap identification
User persona and role mapping
Integration touchpoint inventory (MDM, SAP, transparency reporting)
phases.gate: Requirements sign-off — no new scope after this gate
phases.gotcha: Discovery scope creep is the #1 wave delay. Hard-close requirements at week 4 — late additions go to the next wave or a post-go-live sprint.

phases.overlap_note: Overlaps with late Discovery — start platform configuration for known-scope items in week 3
activities: Platform configuration (profiles, permission sets, page layouts, record types)
Sample limit rules per country
Consent model configuration (opt-in vs opt-out defaults by jurisdiction)
Territory alignment setup
Email template localization and merge field mapping
Content management library structure and restriction rules
Custom solution build for gap items identified in Discovery
phases.gate: Configuration complete — sandbox frozen for testing

activities: Extract from source system (historical data cutoff decision)
Transform and cleanse (field mapping, de-duplication, format normalization)
Dry run load #1 — identify referential integrity issues
Fix data quality issues in source or transform layer
Dry run load #2 — validate all modules
Sample transaction audit trail verification
Consent record validation (country-default compliance check)
phases.gate: Migration validation passes — zero critical errors in dry run #2
phases.gotcha: Plan for 3 dry runs minimum, not 2. The first one always surfaces issues you didn't anticipate. Budget the time upfront rather than scrambling.

activities: E2E Cycle 1: Core workflows (visit creation, sample drop, CLM presentation, email send)
E2E Cycle 2: Integration flows (MDM sync, transparency reporting, adverse event capture)
E2E Cycle 3: Edge cases and regression (offline sync, cross-border scenarios, territory realignment)
Performance testing at target data volumes
Mobile device testing (iPad + iPhone for field reps, web for managers)
Defect triage and resolution between cycles
phases.gate: E2E exit criteria met — all P1/P2 defects resolved, P3 deferred with workarounds documented
phases.gotcha: Never skip E2E Cycle 3. The offline sync and cross-border edge cases are where you find the compliance-impacting bugs that would hit production.

activities: BAT preparation (test scripts, test data, user account provisioning)
BAT execution with business stakeholders from each country
Country-specific regulatory scenario validation
Business process sign-off by country leads
Defect resolution for BAT-found issues
Go/No-Go decision checkpoint
phases.gate: Business sign-off — country leads confirm readiness
phases.gotcha: BAT is not optional. SI teams that skip BAT and go straight from E2E to deployment face 3x the post-go-live support tickets.

activities: Production environment preparation
Final data migration (delta load from cutover date)
Smoke test in production (Day 1 checklist per user role)
Train-the-trainer sessions (2 weeks before end-user training)
End-user training by country (virtual + in-person for first wave)
Hypercare support setup (dedicated support team for 4-6 weeks post-go-live)
Knowledge transfer to BAU support team
phases.gotcha: Train-the-trainer MUST happen before end-user training. Sending untrained trainers to deliver sessions is the fastest way to erode field rep confidence in the new platform.

pilot_wave.name: Pilot Wave (12-14 weeks)
pilot_wave.description: Accelerated timeline for a 2-3 country pilot that validates the platform before the full wave program begins. Recommended as Wave 0 for enterprise deployments.

activities: Select 2-3 pilot countries (include one complex regulatory market)
Define success criteria (Day 1 smoke test pass rate, sync performance, user adoption target)
Baseline platform configuration from prior implementation or reference architecture
Identify pilot champions in each country
Platform configuration for pilot countries
Data migration dry run with pilot country data subset
Integration setup for pilot scope (MDM, transparency if applicable)
Custom solution build for pilot-specific gaps
Combined E2E + BAT (smaller scope allows combining)
Pilot user acceptance with country champions
Sync performance benchmarking with realistic data volumes
Defect resolution
Pilot go-live
Intensive hypercare (daily standups with pilot users)
Lessons learned documentation (what to change for full waves)
Platform optimization based on pilot feedback
Decision: proceed to Wave 1 or iterate pilot
phases.gate: Pilot success criteria met — program proceeds to Wave 1
phases.gotcha: The pilot's real purpose is to find what you got wrong in configuration and data migration. If the pilot surfaces zero surprises, you're not looking hard enough.

us_compliance_wave.name: US Compliance Wave (20-24 weeks)
us_compliance_wave.description: Extended timeline specifically for US deployments due to state-by-state regulatory complexity. Should never be combined with other countries except Canada.

activities: 50-state sample distribution licensing inventory
DEA registration validation requirements
State-specific NP/PA prescriptive authority rules
California furnishing number requirements
Vermont prescriber confidentiality rules
Sunshine Act transparency reporting configuration
State gift and meals regulations mapping
PDMA audit trail requirements finalization
phases.gate: Regulatory matrix signed off by compliance team

activities: License validation rules per state
Sample limit framework configuration (federal + state overlays)
Transparency reporting integration (aggregate spend, meal tracking)
Custom license expiration alert thresholds (90/60/30 day)
Controlled substance workflows (Schedule II-V handling)
Platform configuration (profiles, layouts, territory alignment)
Account and HCP data migration with NPI validation
Historical sample transaction migration with PDMA audit trail preservation
License and credential data migration with expiration date validation
Transparency reporting historical data (if mid-year migration — requires split-year handling)
3 dry run cycles minimum
phases.gotcha: Mid-year US migrations require split-year transparency reporting. Both source and target systems must contribute to the annual Sunshine Act filing. Plan for this or schedule the cutover for January.

activities: Standard E2E testing (3 cycles)
Compliance scenario testing (sampling across state boundaries, DEA validation, license expiration blocking)
Sunshine Act report generation and validation
Cross-border Canada scenarios (if Canada is in scope)
BAT with US compliance team and field leadership
Regulatory sign-off (legal, compliance, medical affairs)
Production deployment
Extended hypercare (6-8 weeks for US due to complexity)
First Sunshine Act reporting cycle validation in production

japan_standalone_wave.name: Japan Standalone Wave (20-24 weeks)
japan_standalone_wave.description: Dedicated timeline for Japan deployments. Japan is always standalone due to APPI, PMDA, and full CJK localization requirements.

activities: APPI data handling requirements mapping
PMDA pharmaceutical regulations review
Full Japanese localization scope (kanji, hiragana, katakana across all UI elements)
Japan-specific business process mapping (HQ-driven vs field-driven differences)
Local stakeholder alignment (Japan country lead, local IT, compliance)
Identify Japan-specific integrations (local MDM, Japan-specific transparency requirements)
Full UI string translation and review (professional translation + in-context review)
CJK character validation across all form fields, reports, and PDF exports
Japan-specific sample rules and limit configuration
APPI consent model implementation
Custom solution build for Japan-specific workflows
Platform configuration with Japan-specific layouts and record types
phases.gotcha: Machine translation is not sufficient for Japan. Budget for professional translators with pharma domain expertise, plus a review cycle with local business users. Mistranslated pharmaceutical terms are a compliance risk.

activities: Data migration with CJK character integrity validation
3 dry run cycles with full localization verification
E2E testing with Japanese-language test scripts
Device testing on Japan-standard iPad models
Compliance scenario testing (APPI, PMDA)
BAT with Japan stakeholders (in-person preferred)
Training material localization and train-the-trainer (local trainers required)
End-user training in Japanese
Production deployment
Extended hypercare with Japan-timezone support coverage
phases.gate: Japan go-live with local stakeholder sign-off
phases.gotcha: Train-the-trainer won't work for Japan without local cultural context. Plan for local trainers, not fly-in trainers from other regions.

cross_wave_activities.description: Activities that span across waves and must be managed at the program level, not the wave level.

activities.name: Parallel Discovery
activities.rule: Start the next wave's Discovery phase during the current wave's E2E Testing. This keeps the program pipeline flowing without dead time between waves.

activities.name: Global Design Authority
activities.rule: Maintain a central configuration governance board that reviews wave-specific customizations against the global template. Prevent configuration drift between waves that makes future upgrades painful.

activities.name: Stabilization Window
activities.rule: Minimum 3-month gap between wave go-lives. This is non-negotiable — it provides time for hypercare, lessons learned, and platform optimization before the next wave adds load.

activities.name: Regression Testing
activities.rule: Every wave must include regression testing of prior-wave countries. A Wave 3 change should never break Wave 1 users. Budget for automated regression suite maintenance starting from Wave 2.

activities.name: Release Alignment
activities.rule: Align wave go-lives with the platform's release calendar. Going live the week before a major platform release is a recipe for compounded risk. Target mid-release-cycle go-lives.

activities.name: SI Bench Rotation
activities.rule: Retain at least 30% of the SI team across waves to preserve institutional knowledge. Full team rotation between waves loses hard-won configuration and data migration expertise.

anti_patterns.name: Big Bang Global
anti_patterns.description: Attempting to deploy to all countries simultaneously. This approach has a near-100% failure rate for deployments over 10 countries. Every global pharma that tried this in the last decade has either rolled back or spent 2x the budget on post-go-live remediation.

anti_patterns.name: US First
anti_patterns.description: Making the US the first wave. US regulatory complexity (50-state licensing, Sunshine Act, PDMA, DEA) makes it the worst possible pilot market. Always deploy to simpler markets first to stabilize the platform.

anti_patterns.name: Japan Bundled
anti_patterns.description: Bundling Japan with other APAC countries. APPI compliance, PMDA requirements, and full CJK localization demand dedicated resources. When bundled, either Japan gets shortchanged or the other APAC countries slip.

anti_patterns.name: Skip the Pilot
anti_patterns.description: Going straight to full Wave 1 without a pilot. The pilot finds configuration and data migration issues at manageable scale. Skipping it means finding these issues at full production scale.

anti_patterns.name: Zero Stabilization Gap
anti_patterns.description: Scheduling the next wave immediately after go-live with no stabilization period. Hypercare issues from Wave N bleed into Wave N+1 preparation, degrading both.

anti_patterns.name: Single-Language BAT
anti_patterns.description: Running BAT only in English for non-English markets. Localization bugs are invisible in English BAT scripts. Run BAT in the local language for every country.
